CAP-CT Program Coordinator
jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Function Summary

Involves analytical studies on a variety of policies, projects, programs and issues in support of a function, research initiative, program and / or organizational unit, or in research of new or changing systems and programs. Assists in policy and program planning, development, administration, management and implementation; interprets, monitors and analyzes information regarding policies and procedures and provides consultative services to department administrators and other stakeholders.

Generic Scope

Professional who applies acquired job skills, policies, and procedures to complete substantive assignments / projects / tasks of moderate scope and complexity; exercises judgment within defined guidelines and practices to determine appropriate action.

Custom Scope

The UCSF Division of Geriatrics seeks to recruit a full-time Program Coordinator
to support the implementation and operational ownership of a Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) funded program, Caregivers as Partners in Care Teams (CAP-CT). This position reports to the Program Director and supports/leads a wide-range of project operations and coordination tasks. The Program Coordinator will perform a broad range of duties that will require analytical, organizational, communication, technical, and coordination skills. Specific duties include: coordinating and maintaining project timelines and deliverables, assisting with researching and applying relevant policies, data collection, management, analyses and reporting, preparing and updating program materials/protocols/procedures, coordinating meeting schedules/agendas/minutes, drafting and updating documents, making program-related purchases and submitting expense reports, conducting literature searches/reviews, and supporting manuscript preparation/scholarly dissemination. The Program Coordinator will additionally function as a subject matter expert and provide oversight and direction on learning management systems, manage digital education platforms, CE/CME accreditation coordination, analytics reporting, marketing communications, website management, and operational support across multiple projects and conferences. This position requires the ability to be proactive, resourceful and efficient, with a high level of flexibility. An ideal candidate will be able to work independently with minimal supervision, balances multiple competing priorities at any given time, and is intellectually curious, willing to learn new skills and a problem-solver. The Program Coordinator may be required to provide the same level of support across projects/programs where there is a need.

Department Overview

The Division of Geriatrics’ work is grounded in a deep commitment to and respect for older persons from diverse backgrounds and lived experiences. We are specialists in aging. Our expertise is in optimizing the health of older individuals. We work in the community and on virtually every UCSF campus – Parnassus, San Francisco VA Health Care System, Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, Mission Bay, and UCSF Center for Geriatric Care. The Division has over 130 employees including faculty, volunteer clinical faculty, fellows, staff, student interns and volunteers. We are deeply committed to, and will champion, diversity, equity and inclusion as our core mission. We will nurture and grow a culture in which everyone from all backgrounds is welcomed, supported, respected, and valued!

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

At least 1 year of relevant experience.
Working knowledge of common organization- or research-specific and other computer application programs.
Proficient in communication and interpersonal skills to communicate effectively, both verbally and in writing.
Proficient in ability to use discretion and maintain all confidentiality.
Demonstrates ability to use sound judgment in responding to issues and concerns.
Demonstrates ability to analyze, research and synthesize large amounts of data with strong attention to detail.
Proficient in ability to multi-task with demanding timeframes.
Experience in using Qualtrics/REDCap/other surveying platforms.
Proficient in MS Suite (Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel, Word, etc.)
Proficient with Continuing Medical Education (CME) and Learning Management System (LMS).
Experience working with consumers of educational courses/academic institutions.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in public health or research administration, e.g. working on state contracts, NIH programs, or working in an academic institution.
Previous experience using project management tools and software, website management and managing social media platforms.

Required Education

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training.

Job Summary

Project Coordinator provides complex administrative support to various members of the project team under the direction of the Office Manager. The Project Coordinator I will be responsible for project oversight and coordination of all its stages from inception to completion by inputting data, tracking, and monitoring control points and program updates. Additional responsibilities include assisting with document management and tracking progress for program estimates.

Intake new leads and jobs, entering all information across platforms to maintain a single, accurate source of data.

Prepare job files and organize paperwork accurately using Salesforce.
Transfer and upload photos into specific files to forward to corporate staff.
Assist with reconciliation and sending billing reports to accounting staff by monthly deadlines and handle billing exceptions.
Generate requests to ensure promptness on estimates.
Attend all appropriate company training and monthly Admin Program meetings.
Execute administrative support functions and perform special project assistance as needed.

Qualifications And Experience

High School Diploma or equivalent.
Minimum of 1 year of experience in a coordinator or administrative role.
Construction industry experience preferred.
Experience working in Salesforce, including generating reports (preferred).
TRAVEL & WORKING CONDITIONS
Travel is minimal for this position.
This position requires sitting for long periods of time and looking at monitors along with typing for extended periods of time.
This position may require occasional flexibility in schedule to address urgent or time-sensitive employee relations matters.
Work is performed in a professional office environment.

jobs.title: Project Coordinator
jobs.description:
SitelogIQ
is a rapidly growing engineering and construction company focused on making buildings better. We provide planning, design, and management solutions for organizations that want efficient and sustainable building environments that are healthier and safer for their occupants.

Our Project Coordinator
will be an in-office role working out of our West Business Unit
, located in Sacramento, CA
. As a Project Coordinator at SitelogIQ
, you'll play a key role in supporting the successful delivery of energy, infrastructure, and construction projects that improve schools, healthcare facilities, and communities. Working alongside Project Managers, engineers, subcontractors, and clients, you'll help keep projects organized, compliant, and moving forward from kickoff through closeout. This is an excellent opportunity for a detail-oriented professional who enjoys solving problems, coordinating multiple priorities, and wants to build a career in project management, construction operations, or the energy services industry.

Target Hourly:
$28/hour - $34/hour+ depending on experience

Project Coordinator Responsibilities

Coordination

Represent SitelogIQ (SIQ) professionally and with utmost courtesy, precision, positivity, respect, and attention to detail when engaging with clients, subcontractors, and vendors.
Demonstrate effective and proactive communication skills, fostering clear interactions within our internal teams and in our dealings with external customers, vendors, and subcontractors.
Advocate for the delivery of exceptional customer service.
Maintain a state of equilibrium when engaging with multiple stakeholders, ensuring that customer expectations are met while working with efficiency and effectiveness.
Collaborate seamlessly with various SIQ functional teams encompassing operations, business development, and engineering.
Serve as the primary resource for all team members regarding operational processes and historical information.
Act as the cohesive force that binds our team together.
Supply development teams with updated cost of sales information.
Follow up with subcontractors to provide additional project information and ensure current compliance requirements are documented, including certificates of insurance, bonds, and certified payroll.

Administration

Strictly adhere to regulatory and industry safety standards, following the guidelines outlined in the SafetyIQ Manual, and meticulously document compliance with SafetyIQ and safety training.
Create development projects in SitelogIQ’s ERP and Construction Management systems, Acumatica and Procore.
Complete contract exhibits accurately.
Facilitate project launch meetings and set up initial project documentation, including the transition of development projects to the work-in-progress status in both Acumatica and Procore.
Create and store Notice to Proceed documentation for Project Managers.
Procure, obtain, and safely store proof of payment, performance bonds, and insurance.
Maintain records of preliminary notices.
Review, organize, store, and retrieve critical documents such as executed contracts, compliance and performance documentation, and offer guidance to team members on effective storage of meeting minutes, proposals, memos, emails, and other forms of correspondence.
Verify the registration of projects with the Department of Industrial Relations.
Confirm the receipt and audit of all certified payroll reporting submissions.
Facilitate document execution, such as prime contracts, subcontracts, or change orders, through DocuSign.
Compile, organize, and document all aspects of completion documentation, including certification of completion, product literature, operations and maintenance instructions, training materials, and warranty statements.

Procurement

Collect the necessary information required by the accounting department for new vendor or customer accounts in Acumatica.
Validate and process lead generation payments through Accounts Payable.
Secure any required permits.
Supply Project Managers with subcontract agreement numbers for tracking in Acumatica.
Adjust subcontract values according to executed change order documentation.
Supply project managers with purchase order numbers for mechanical and solar equipment orders upon receipt of relevant order documentation. Work with corporate accounting department to reconcile purchase orders for adjustments to sales tax, change directives from Project Managers, and to periodically close out purchase orders.
Offer essential support and set up recurring payments for site logistics, including the procurement of modular storage, temporary fencing, portable toilets, hand wash stations, disposal services, and other minor site requirements.
Successfully complete the procurement process and diligently document it within SitelogIQ's ERP system.
Fulfill any other job duties as assigned in a productive manner.

Project Coordinator Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Business, or a related field, or 3+ years of equivalent experience supporting a team in construction management or accounting preferred.
Completion of or willingness to obtain OSHA10 certification (covered by the company) within one year.
CA Department of Education Federal and State Background Clearances are mandatory.
Experience working in environments involving multiple stakeholders.
Proficiency in using the MS Office Suite, including MS Project, as well as web-based and smartphone applications. Knowledge of construction technology and management software, with preference for familiarity with Procore and Acumatica.
Working knowledge of job cost accounting and percentage-of-completion (WIP) revenue recognition principles as applied to construction, ESCO, and renewable energy projects.
Experience reviewing subcontractor pay applications and reconciling retention, lien releases, and progress billing (e.g., AIA G702/G703) against contract terms.
Ability to track budget-to-actual variances at the project level and flag cost overruns or margin erosion for Project Manager and Finance review.
Familiarity with change order cost impact analysis and updating project budgets and forecasts in Acumatica accordingly.
Understanding of sales and use tax treatment on construction materials and equipment purchases.
Familiarity with California Regulatory agencies, including DIR, is a plus.

Physical Requirements

Physical capability to climb ladders and stairs, comfortably lift 40+ pounds, and stand for extended periods.

No Agencies, please

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.**

Benefits

We offer a highly competitive salary, and comprehensive benefits, including:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Disability and life insurance
401K
Flexible time off
Paid holidays including a day off in the month of your birthday
Tuition reimbursement
Opportunities to join our affinity groups, Veterans and Allies Leadership Organization or Women Inspiring & Strengthening Everyone
Opportunities to give back to our local communities through organized events or fundraisers

More About SitelogIQ

At SitelogIQ, we’re focused on creating a great environment for our team first so that it is more energizing and rewarding to focus on creating great customer experience. That’s what we call a win-win.

We partner with clients in K-12 school districts, higher ed, local and state government, healthcare, commercial real estate, automotive dealerships, and manufacturing and distribution to optimize energy efficiency, improve indoor air quality, address lighting, and improve customer experience. With offices across the country, it’s rewarding to make a difference in the communities where our teammates live and work.

SitelogIQ is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-Verify.

jobs.title: Program Coordinator - Night Shift
jobs.description:
Who We Are

At ERC Pathlight, we’re on a mission to change lives—and we’re looking for people who feel called to do the same.

As one of the nation’s leading treatment providers for eating disorders and mood, anxiety, and trauma-related conditions, we bring innovative, evidence-based, and deeply compassionate care to patients across the country. With multiple locations nationwide and extensive virtual programming, we meet patients exactly where they are and help them move toward lasting recovery.

Founded in 2008 by renowned psychiatrists and psychologists, ERC Pathlight now supports more than 6,000 patients each year. And as the need for world-class mental health care continues to rise, our commitment is stronger than ever: to expand access, elevate the standard of care, and empower every patient to rebuild their life with dignity and hope.

Why Join Us

When you join ERC Pathlight, you become part of a team that shows up every day to make a real difference. You’ll work alongside passionate clinicians, dedicated support staff, and mission-driven leaders who believe in collaboration, growth, and doing the right thing—always.

Here, your work matters. Your ideas matter. You
matter.

If you’re energized by purpose, motivated by impact, and ready to help transform the future of mental health treatment, you belong here.

Come build hope. Come save lives. Come grow with us.

The Program Coordinator (PC I, PC II, PC III) is responsible for the direct care of inpatient, residential, and partial hospitalization patients by providing patient supervision and support. The PCs provide structure and boundaries for our patients. They provide bathroom and milieu support as well as contribute to the implementation of therapeutic programming which may include care delivery and program documentation. The PCs provide mealtime support, supporting patients with their dietary needs, and supervising patients at meals and snacks.

The PC Should Be Able To

Be willing and able to work at all ERC Pathlight local sites as assigned
Be compliant with certification and regulatory requirements for each practice location
Maintain a flexible schedule to meet organizational staffing needs
Be available to work weekends and holidays as required
Be available to work on-call shifts based on business needs, in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local labor laws

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Milieu Management, including (but not limited to) the following:
Maintains daily program structure by following program schedule
Completes observation rounds and safety checks as ordered by physician
Works with patients on de-escalation and implementing coping skills per treatment plan
Conducts room searches and luggage searches

Involves analytical studies on a variety of policies, projects, programs and issues in support of a function, research initiative, program and / or organizational unit, or in research of new or changing systems and programs. Professional who applies acquired job skills, policies, and procedures to complete substantive assignments / projects / tasks of moderate scope and complexity; exercises judgment within defined guidelines and practices to determine appropriate action.

The UCSF Division of Geriatrics seeks to recruit a full-time Program Coordinator
to support the implementation and operational ownership of a Department of Health and Human Services (DHHS) funded program, Caregivers as Partners in Care Teams (CAP-CT). This position reports to the Program Director and supports/leads a wide-range of project operations and coordination tasks. The Program Coordinator will perform a broad range of duties that will require analytical, organizational, communication, technical, and coordination skills. Specific duties include: coordinating and maintaining project timelines and deliverables, assisting with researching and applying relevant policies, data collection, management, analyses and reporting, preparing and updating program materials/protocols/procedures, coordinating meeting schedules/agendas/minutes, drafting and updating documents, making program-related purchases and submitting expense reports, conducting literature searches/reviews, and supporting manuscript preparation/scholarly dissemination. The Program Coordinator will additionally function as a subject matter expert and provide oversight and direction on learning management systems, manage digital education platforms, CE/CME accreditation coordination, analytics reporting, marketing communications, website management, and operational support across multiple projects and conferences. This position requires the ability to be proactive, resourceful and efficient, with a high level of flexibility. An ideal candidate will be able to work independently with minimal supervision, balances multiple competing priorities at any given time, and is intellectually curious, willing to learn new skills and a problem-solver. The Program Coordinator may be required to provide the same level of support across projects/programs where there is a need.

The Division of Geriatrics’ work is grounded in a deep commitment to and respect for older persons from diverse backgrounds and lived experiences. We are specialists in aging. We work in the community and on virtually every UCSF campus – Parnassus, San Francisco VA Health Care System, Zuckerberg San Francisco General Hospital, Mission Bay, and UCSF Center for Geriatric Care. The Division has over 130 employees including faculty, volunteer clinical faculty, fellows, staff, student interns and volunteers. We will nurture and grow a culture in which everyone from all backgrounds is welcomed, supported, respected, and valued!

Previous experience using project management tools and software, website management and managing social media platforms.

Follow site-specific safety requirements, environmental regulations, standard operating procedures, and established safe work practices.

Respond promptly to system alarms, shutdowns, and operational issues, including after-hours and weekend events while on call.

Basic mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.

Strong attention to detail, safety, documentation, and data accuracy.
Ability to work independently when appropriately trained and to collaborate effectively with the project team.
Ability to work outdoors in varying terrain and weather conditions.
Ability to stand for extended periods and lift and carry up to 50 pounds, including field equipment, supplies, and PPE.

Previous internship, military, laboratory, field, construction, utilities, mechanical, or water treatment experience.

OSHA, HAZWOPER, water treatment, first aid, or other relevant safety and technical training.

new_jobs.title: Project Coordinator, Contract Services
new_jobs.description:
At the MBTA, we envision a thriving region enabled by a best-in-class transit system. Our mission is to serve the public by providing safe, reliable, and accessible transportation. MBTA’s core values are built around safety, service, equity, sustainability, culture, and accessibility, and each employee that works for the MBTA performs their roles based on our vision, mission, and values. This includes attendance, participation, and contribution in local safety committee meetings as needed.

Job Summary

Contract Services is responsible for the procurement and administration of professional services and construction contracts, including alternative delivery methods such as Construction Management at Risk and Design Build. The group supports the MBTA's multi-billion-dollar Capital Investment Plan (CIP) throughout the full delivery lifecycle, from contract procurement, contract administration including management of contract changes and amendments, invoice review and payment processing, dispute resolution to contract closeout.

The Project Coordinator will assist Contract Services teams by coordinating contractual actions and related business processes, supporting procurement, contract administration, change management, invoice review and payment processing, document control, stakeholder communication, and contract closeout. The role provides administrative and project coordination support to ensure contracts are executed efficiently, comply with MBTA policies and applicable regulations, and contribute to the successful delivery of the CIP.

Duties & Responsibilities

Assist with preparing solicitation documents for professional services and construction contracts for state-funded and/or federally funded capital projects, in accordance with applicable agency policies and procedures.
Assist with contractor, consultant, and vendor qualification, prequalification, and compliance processes in accordance with agency policies and procurement requirements.
Advertise and disseminate procurement opportunities through agency-approved electronic procurement systems, including all statutorily required and agency-designated external notification channels.
Assist with the administration of payments to consultants, designers, contractors, and third party vendors, including receiving, tracking, and processing invoices and vouchers through agency financial and contract management systems.
Create and maintain project, procurement, and contract documents and records, including bidder/proposer lists, solicitation documentation, and contract communications such as salary increase requests, agenda, and notifications, etc., ensuring that they are accurate and up to date.
Assist with documenting and tracking contractor's work directives, claims, payment invoices, risk reallocations, and/or change orders.
Assist Risk Management to track, log and maintain the authority’s Insurance database and related compliance documentation.
Assist with preparing, processing, tracking, and maintaining contract modifications and related contract actions, including amendments, task orders, work orders, change orders, work directives, and other administrative actions.
Assist in the preparation, formatting, and issuance of procurement and contract documents, letters including notices to proceed and other official communications to consultants or contractors.
Assist in the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and manuals, and in updating.
MBTA-related policies and procedures based on Federal Transit Administration (FTA) Regulations and Best Practices as well as State Procurement Laws.
Coordinate tasks with Capital Programs personnel, including contract administration staff and other project coordinators, as required.
Prepare project-related correspondence, reports, charts, and presentations using MS Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), using data extracted from Project and Financial Management information systems or databases.
Analyze contracts to ensure compliance with state and federal laws and regulations. Review submitted project documentation and ensure accuracy per MBTA standard operating procedures.
Analyze, review, correct, and administer systems data across Project Management Information Systems (PMIS), and Capital Management System (CMS), and Financial Information Systems (FMIS) platforms to directly support and execute a wide spectrum of team-specific functions and workflows.
Assist in Federal, State, and Agency Audits.
Coordinate tasks within the Engineering and Capital Division and other MBTA departments, including but not limited to Railroad Operations, Environmental, and Safety. Proactively follow-up with Project Managers and Capital Support Staff on pending contract actions, change-related actions, and closeout documentation. Communicate with external third parties, including but not limited to contractors and/or consultants, as necessary.
Organize and prioritize workload, assisting Project Manager(s), Contract Services staff and other Capital Programs Support staff in identifying project and process needs/requirements.
Organize and maintain effective means to interpret, present, and communicate project information at internal and external meetings with project office staff, change order management, and other MBTA departments and public agencies.
Organize, schedule, and facilitate meetings with internal and external stakeholders, maintain accurate meeting documentation, and track action items. Attend on-and-off-site meetings, as necessary.
Contribute to and support the achievement of goals, objectives, and strategic priorities established by Contract Services, within the Capital Program Support Group and the Engineering and Capital Division.
Work independently in addressing tasks in a time-sensitive environment. Follow up on actions required for task completion while seeking guidance as necessary.
Respond to each inquiry, whether from a customer, vendor or co-worker in a professional and courteous manner.
Support the onboarding, training, and mentoring of new and existing team members, by providing guidance and knowledge transfer as needed.
Perform other related duties and projects that may be assigned.

Additional responsibilities may include a focus on one or more departments or locations. See applicable addendum for department or location-specific functions.

Minimum Requirements & Qualifications

A Bachelor's Degree from an accredited institution.
Four (4) years of experience in project coordination and administration.
Proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, Database and PowerPoint.
Self-starter with the ability to work productively independently and as part of a team.
Excellent organizational, analytical, confidentiality, multi-tasking, time management and interpersonal skills.
Ability to effectively communicate with customers, employees and vendors.
The ability to work effectively with a diverse workforce.
Effective and professional written and communication skills.

Substitutions

A High School Diploma or GED with an additional seven (7) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
An associate degree from an accredited institution with an additional three (3) years of directly related experience substitutes for the bachelor’s degree requirement.
A master’s degree in a related subject substitute for two (2) years of general experience.
A nationally recognized certification, or statewide/professional certification in a related field substitutes for one year of experience.

Preferred Experience & Skills

A Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Architecture, Business Administration or a related field from an accredited institution.
Experience providing project support in a public sector, transit, and/or facilities environment.

Job Conditions

Ability to effectively read, comprehend, communicate, and respond to instructions, orders, signs, notices, inquiries, etc. in English.
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age, except if participating in an approved high school internship / co-op program.
Ability to commute to assigned work locations in the Boston, MA metro area, as required by the role.
Ability to provide internal and external customers with courteous and professional experiences.
Ability to work effectively, independently, and as part of a diverse workforce team (or supervise, if required).
Ability to uphold the rights and interests of the MBTA while building and maintaining effective relationships with employees and co-workers.
Ability to adhere to rules, regulations, collective bargaining agreements (if applicable), and policies of the MBTA, including the EEO, anti-discrimination, anti-harassment, and anti-retaliation policies.
Have a satisfactory work record for the two (2) years immediately prior to the closing date of this posting (unless if current student or recent graduate), including overall employment, job performance, discipline, and safety records (infractions and/or offenses occurring after the closing of the posting and before the filling of a vacancy may preclude a candidate from consideration for selection).
Ability to pass a Criminal Offender Record Information (CORI) check, comprehensive background screening, and / or medical Clinic screening, potentially including physical examination and drug and alcohol screenings.
Ability to work all shifts and / or locations assigned, directed, or necessary for this position, including (for some transit / operations roles) up to twenty-four (24) hours per day, seven (7) days per week as necessary to accommodate severe weather conditions, emergencies, or any other circumstances that may potentially impact service or the safety of service.
